title: Field Sales Copilots
answer: Drugmakers are building assistants that brief representatives before each visit, drawing on a doctor's specialty, prescribing history and past engagement and suggesting tailored messages. Sanofi chose Snowflake's data cloud and Cortex AI to build such tools.

reading.body:
Sanofi chose Snowflake's data cloud and Cortex AI to build field sales copilots that brief representatives before each visit.

The pattern is a briefing assistant rather than a chatbot. It draws on a doctor's specialty, prescribing history and past engagement, then suggests tailored messages. The value sits in assembling context a representative would otherwise gather by hand, and the model is the last step, not the first.

For AI specifically, this is a data-placement decision before it is a model decision. Sanofi picked a data cloud and built on the AI layer inside it, which keeps the prescribing and engagement history in the same place the assistant reads from. The governance note follows from that: suggested messages should come only from approved materials and be logged like any other promotional interaction.

The data covers one named company and one named platform. It does not say how many representatives use the tool, what it cost, whether it improved any commercial outcome, or how the briefing is validated before a visit. Nothing here speaks to compute, buildings, or power, so no claim about the grid can be drawn from it.

explainer:
Before a visit, a representative traditionally reviews call notes, prescribing data and approved materials to decide what to discuss. Copilots automate that preparation, assembling a brief and suggesting topics and materials suited to the doctor's interests and past engagement, and afterwards help log the call.

Building them requires connecting CRM, commercial data and content systems, which is why drugmakers are pairing data platforms with AI services. The compliance requirements are the same as for any promotional activity: suggestions must come from approved materials, recommendations must respect the label, and interactions must be recorded.
